name: Comoros
summary: Volcanic islands between Mozambique and Madagascar, once Swahili sultanates; French colony until 1975, when three islands chose independence and Mayotte stayed French. Many coups followed.

knownFor.label: Ylang-ylang
knownFor.note: Flower oil for perfume; a top producer.

knownFor.label: Grand mariage
knownFor.note: Lavish wedding custom that raises status.

location.value: Three major islands (Grande Comore, Anjouan, Mohéli) and smaller ones; area 1,659 km² in the text and island table but 2,235 km² in the infobox.

terrain.value: Volcanic islands with steep mountains; Mount Karthala is one of the world’s largest active volcanoes.

climate.value: Tropical, with a rainy season and cyclones.

resources.value: Vanilla, cloves and ylang-ylang (a top producer for perfume).

disasters.value: Volcanic eruptions of Mount Karthala and cyclones have hit the islands.

population.value: 944,388 in a 2026 estimate; 758,316 at the 2017 census.

urbanisation.value: Most people live in and around the capital.

disease.value: Good basic health care; rising diabetes.

migration.value: Many people go to Mayotte and France; remittances are vital.

economicBase.value: Agriculture was 36.6% of GDP in 2024 and cloves were 64.9% of exports in 2023; the Comoros supplies about 80% of the world’s ylang-ylang; remittances were around 20% of GDP in 2023.

tradeRoutes.value: Exports of spices and perfume oils by sea.

wealth.value: A lower-middle-income country with widespread poverty.

moneyAndTax.value: The Comorian franc, pegged to the euro and backed by France.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

keyRulers.value: Ahmed Abdallah proclaimed independence on 6 July 1975, was removed in a coup on 3 August 1975, returned after the coup of 13 May 1978 and ruled until 1989 when he was reportedly killed. Later and present leaders are not named here.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Comoros (checked 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: Comoros (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Abdallah’s government declared independence on 6 July 1975 and he was deposed later that year; mercenaries led by Robert Denard returned him to power in May 1978 and he was assassinated in November 1989)

succession.value: Elections and about 20 coups or attempts.

institutions.value: Union government; presidency rotated between the islands until 2018.

stability.value: About 20 coups or attempts; Anjouan and Mohéli tried to secede (1997–2001).

eliteConflict.value: Rivalry between islands and political families.

armyAndTech.value: Small army; French mercenaries (Bob Denard) staged several coups.

majorWars.value: More than 20 coups or attempted coups since independence (the 1999 one was the 18th); on 25 March 2008 African Union and Comorian soldiers took rebel-held Anjouan.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Comoros (checked 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: Comoros (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Comorian and African Union troops took Anjouan on 25 March 2008; the page lists coups in 1978, 1995 and 1999 but gives no total count)

territoryChange.value: Mayotte stayed French after the 1974 vote.

alliancesRivals.value: Claims Mayotte, which voted to stay French in 1974 and became a French department in 2011.

inventions.value: No major inventions are recorded; the islands are known for perfume plants such as ylang-ylang.

scienceEducation.value: The University of the Comoros was founded in 2003.

openness.value: Limited by poverty and isolation, with heavy dependence on foreign aid and money sent home.

communicationTransport.value: Ferries and small flights between islands.

religion.value: Islam is the state religion: 99.6% in 2025 (infobox), with Christians 0.3%.

languageWriting.value: Comorian (Shikomori, a Swahili-related language), French and Arabic.

artsArchitecture.value: Swahili-style old towns and mosques; carved doors.

socialStructure.value: Mixed African, Arab and Malagasy descent.

sharedIdentity.value: Strong island loyalties within a Comorian identity.

dailyLife.value: Rice, fish, cassava and coconut; the grand mariage wedding.

neighbours.value: Mozambique, Madagascar and the French island of Mayotte.

ideasReligions.value: Islam and Swahili coastal culture, with Sunni Islam practised by almost everyone.

colonisation.value: French colony (Mayotte 1841, the rest by 1886) until 1975.

riseSignals.value: Three of the islands gained independence in 1975.

peakPeriod.value: Too recent to judge. The page records more than 20 coups or attempted coups since independence and a long dispute over Mayotte.

declineSignals.value: Frequent coups and secession crises, notably in Anjouan in the late 1990s.

outcome.value: Still in existence: independence was proclaimed on 6 July 1975. Azali Assoumani was re-elected in January 2024 in a disputed vote. Comoros still claims Mayotte, which stayed French.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
